# Global burden, economic cost and access to PD care — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Global burden, economic cost and access to PD care. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Definitions

- [statement] WHO reports that levodopa/carbidopa is not accessible, available or affordable everywhere, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-08-09) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Fothergill-Misbah and colleagues found that 81% (38/47) of countries in the WHO African Region included levodopa plus carbidopa or levodopa plus benserazide as a therapeutic alternative on national essential medicines lists, considering any formulation or strength. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-25) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12481222/
- [statement] The Middle East physician survey reported levodopa availability of 98% among its participating countries. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-08) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13380763/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] WHO reports that global estimates in 2019 showed over 8.5 million individuals with Parkinson disease. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-08-09) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease
- [statement] The Global Burden of Disease collaborators estimated 6·1 million individuals with Parkinson disease globally in 2016, with a 95% uncertainty interval of 5·0–7·3 million. (low confidence) (verified as of 2018-11-01) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6191528/
- [statement] Luo and colleagues report that 11.77 million people worldwide had Parkinson disease in 2021, using the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-10) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11757241/
- [statement] The BMJ modelling study projects 25.2 million people living with Parkinson disease worldwide in 2050, with a 95% uncertainty interval of 21.7 to 30.1 million. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-03-05) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40044233/
- [statement] Yang and colleagues estimated the total economic burden of diagnosed Parkinson disease in the United States in 2017 at $51.9 billion. (low confidence) (verified as of 2020-07-09) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7347582/
- [statement] Yang and colleagues projected the total economic burden of Parkinson disease in the United States to surpass $79 billion by 2037. (low confidence) (verified as of 2020-07-09) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7347582/
- [statement] The Lewin Group report estimates a combined economic burden of Parkinson disease and atypical parkinsonism of $82.2 billion in the United States for 2024. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-17) — https://www.michaeljfox.org/sites/default/files/media/document/Economic%20Burden%20of%20Parkinson%E2%80%99s%20and%20Atypical%20Parkinsonism%20in%20the%20United%20States_0.pdf · keywords: Global burden, economic cost and access to PD care · also: https://www.parkinson.org/about-us/news/economic-burden-2024-report
- [statement] Fothergill-Misbah and colleagues state that inclusion of Parkinson disease medicines in national essential medicines lists provides no guarantee of immediate access. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-25) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12481222/
- [statement] WHO’s technical-brief launch news states that globally the prevalence of Parkinson disease has doubled in the past 25 years. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-06-14) — https://www.who.int/news/item/14-06-2022-launch-of-who-s-parkinson-disease-technical-brief
- [statement] The Lewin Group report defines PWPD/AP as people with Parkinson’s disease inclusive of atypical parkinsonism. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-17) — https://www.michaeljfox.org/sites/default/files/media/document/Economic%20Burden%20of%20Parkinson%E2%80%99s%20and%20Atypical%20Parkinsonism%20in%20the%20United%20States_0.pdf

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The Middle East survey authors caution that their data were physician-reported perceptions rather than objective verification, with potential reporting bias and failure to capture within-country variability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-08) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13380763/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The nationwide Nigerian pharmacy survey found that only trihexyphenidyl tablets and biperiden injection were affordable under its study definition. (low confidence) (verified as of 2018-11-16) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6335528/
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation states that annual costs surpassed the $79 billion previously projected for 2037, more than a decade early. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/about-us/news/economic-burden-2024-report
